title: Story-060 fix line (vault.previewRedeem) reverts against the real Tokemak Autopool vaults — ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 deposit() is dead-on-arrival and the migration suite cannot complete
severityNote: Proposed High by auditor: committed remediation for a live user-facing outage (withdrawDisabled(DOLA)==true on mainnet today), and the suite as written strands the migration after leg 1 has moved users into the temp staker. Strict C4 mapping may be Medium (loud failure, no direct asset loss — parked users can withdraw idle funds). severity-classifier to decide.
description: The story-060 fix credits `creditedPrincipal = vault.previewRedeem(sharesReceived)` inside `_acquireShares`; the intent doc prescribed `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)`. The deployment targets are NOT plain ERC4626 vaults: autoDOLA (0x79eB…A54d) and autoUSDC (0xa756…0D35) are Tokemak Autopool proxies whose previewRedeem mutates state internally (withdrawal-queue simulation). Solc compiles the external `view` call as STATICCALL, so the inner state write raises StateChangeDuringStaticCall and consumes all forwarded gas: EVERY `deposit()` into the freshly deployed ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 reverts. Top-level eth_call previewRedeem succeeds (no static frame), which is why off-chain checks and the committed preview JSON never caught it. Downstream, ResetAndRewire's `setYieldStrategy` idle sweep and every Leg2Migration `depositFor -> _routeDeposit -> strategy.deposit` revert: the suite bricks at step 3/4, after leg 1 has drained the original staker into the temp staker, and the underwater-withdraw outage the suite exists to fix remains unfixed. CONSEQUENCE manifests downstream as the reset-step-3 revert and the leg2 dependency; those reset/leg2 mentions are impact evidence for this finding, not separate findings.
evidence: workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditYsSwapDeployStep1.t.sol — 3 passing fork tests at block 25297374: (1) ysDolaV2-equivalent deposit of 1,000 DOLA reverts; (2) ysUsdcV2-equivalent deposit of 1,000 USDC reverts; (3) root-cause isolation: previewRedeem via contract STATICCALL reverts on both vaults while convertToAssets succeeds (autoDOLA convertToAssets(1e18)=1.16799e18, autoUSD=1086674). Trace shows revert at AutopoolETH::previewRedeem with StateChangeDuringStaticCall. side-effects.json postconditionResults[6]. Reset-entry side-effects.json unmodifiedPreview reverts at FIRST setYieldStrategy with StateChangeDuringStaticCall (downstream confirmation).
impact: Migration suite cannot complete; if broadcast in order, users end up parked in the temp staker (funds recoverable via withdraw, zero emissions) with no working path back; the live DOLA withdrawal block persists. New strategy contracts are unusable as deployed.
recommendation: Change the fix to the doc-prescribed `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` (verified static-callable on both Autopools), or cache previewRedeem semantics via a non-view pattern. Re-deploy V2 strategies before any later leg runs. Add a deposit smoke test (1-wei depositAsOwner) or an in-script `try IERC4626(vault).previewRedeem(1e18)` static probe to step-1 preflight so strategy/vault incompatibility fails at deploy time, not mid-migration.
dedupNotes: Canonical raw: deploy F1 (migrate:ys-swap-deploy/idx0). Downstream consequences (reset-step-3 revert, leg2 brick) are folded as impact/evidence here per auditor cross-reference — they are NOT separate findings. NOTE: the SCRIPT-LEVEL amplification of this brick at the reset entry (skip-simulation + non-idempotent ordering + unpaused halt window) is kept as a distinct finding YS-09 (same family, different root cause class: operational non-resumability vs the vault-call bug itself).

title: Leg-1 broadcast is dead on arrival: deployer/owner is not an authorized withdrawer on any of the 3 old strategies, so the first mutating call (skimSurplus) reverts and no suite step grants the permission
location: script/SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-200 (skim calls), :126-138 (preflight checks owner() only); root cause lib/vault/src/AYieldStrategy.sol:461-471 (skimSurplus onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer), :224-229 (modifier), :309 (setWithdrawer, the only grant path). Missing wiring belongs in DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol (step 1) or a leg-1 preflight.
description: `skimSurplus` is gated on the authorizedWithdrawers registry, which is fully separate from owner — the owner is never implicitly authorized. On live state the ONLY authorized withdrawer on YS_DOLA_OLD/YS_USDC_OLD/YS_USDE is the post-replace-sya SYA (0x3C69…8270, wired by ReplaceSYAMainnet step 12); authorizedWithdrawers[OWNER]==false on all three (verified on fork). SkimAndLeg1Migration calls skimSurplus as the owner EOA, and neither this script nor any other story-060 step calls setWithdrawer(OWNER, true). The script's preflight verifies owner() on all three strategies but never checks withdrawer status, so the failure is only discovered at execution. Empirically (fork preview, unmodified script, valid inputs): revert 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers' at IOldYS(YS_DOLA_OLD).skimSurplus. In broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) this would be a real failed mainnet tx and the suite halts at step 2 of 5.
impact: The story-060 migration suite cannot execute as written: step 2 deterministically fails before any migration occurs (fail-safe — no partial state, one wasted failed tx). Migration of the buggy DOLA/USDC strategies is blocked until out-of-band setWithdrawer transactions are crafted manually.
evidence: side-effects.json executed[1] (exact revert), preconditionResults (missing check), fork reads: authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER)==false x3, authorizedWithdrawers(SYA)==true x3 on 0x90ce…7F9, 0x90af…470, 0xaC2e…f95. grep over all 5 suite scripts: zero setWithdrawer calls. Fork fixup (setWithdrawer(OWNER,true) x3 from the strategies' owner) lets preview and broadcast-equivalent complete end-to-end. side-effects.json clusterChecks[0].
recommendation: Add `setWithdrawer(OWNER_ADDRESS, true)` on the three old strategies to step 1 (inside the broadcast block, before the skims; the strategies' owner is the same signing EOA) and revoke in PostMigrationCleanup, OR route the skim through the SYA's own collection entry point. Add a preflight `require(authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER_ADDRESS))` so the script refuses to broadcast into a guaranteed failure.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED two raw candidates with one root cause: deploy F2 (migrate:ys-swap-deploy/idx1) and leg1 idx0. Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1 (the script that actually reverts at its first mutation). The deploy-entry instance (F2) raised it as a forward-looking cluster flag; merged here. Per-entryPoint fingerprint namespacing means these would not auto-collide, but they share root cause MissingWithdrawerAuthorization and are presented as one finding.

title: Post-migration yield collection silently severed: SYA still points at the old strategies and is never authorized as withdrawer on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 — staker DOLA/USDC yield becomes uncollectable and the 10% buffer is dead config; the cleanup gate never verifies it
location: DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol:185-193 (root cause); absence confirmed across ResetAndRewire.s.sol and PostMigrationCleanup.s.sol; missing verification at PostMigrationCleanup.s.sol:137-246
description: The live yield pipeline is: strategies -> SYA.skimSurplus (SYA is the only authorized withdrawer) -> Phlimbo/NFT-minter. The new SYA (0x3C69…8270) has an on-chain strategy list [YS_DOLA_OLD, YS_USDE, YS_USDC_OLD] and replace-sya granted it withdrawer ONLY on those old strategies. The deploy script wires the V2 strategies' clients and buffers but never calls `setWithdrawer(SYA, true)`, and no story-060 sibling re-points the SYA (`addYieldStrategy(ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2)` / removal of the old entries). After migration completes, all staker DOLA/USDC principal sits in V2 strategies whose surplus nothing can skim: protocol yield to Phlimbo/NFT holders from these pools silently stops, and the 10% set-aside buffer configured by this script can never trigger. Unlike YS-01/YS-02 this failure is SILENT. SEPARATELY, the PostMigrationCleanup 'verify final state' step (the LAST gate of the suite) checks V2 principal, buffer SIZE and buffer RECIPIENT but never verifies the SYA was repointed/registered as a client on the V2 strategies — it green-lights this dead-buffer config rather than catching it.
evidence: Fork reads: SYA.getYieldStrategies() == [0x90ce…7F9, 0xaC2e…f95, 0x90af…470]; ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2.authorizedWithdrawers(SYA) == false (suite greps clean for setWithdrawer). side-effects.json clusterChecks[1]. Cleanup script L212-232 asserts setAsideBufferSize==10 / recipient==original but contains no SYA reference anywhere in the file (cleanup-entry idx2). closure-manifest cluster skipped-step 'SYA NOT REWIRED' (sharedAddresses ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2/old strategies/SYA); sibling replace-sya (25% buffer on OLD strategies).
impact: Permanent (until manual owner intervention) loss of yield collection for the two largest staker pools post-migration; buffer protection configured at deploy time is unreachable; the finalizer declares the end-state good while a material yield-routing leg is unwired.
recommendation: Extend the suite (cleanup step or a dedicated rewire) to: ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2.setWithdrawer(SYA, true); SYA.addYieldStrategy(ysDolaV2, DOLA) + addYieldStrategy(ysUsdcV2, USDC); remove/retire the old strategy entries once the minter's position is resolved (see YS-12). ADD a cleanup verify that the SYA (and any minter client) is a registered client on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 with the intended buffer, OR explicitly document in the runbook that SYA re-wiring is a required follow-up the cleanup deliberately does not cover, with a loud console warning. Do not assert a buffer size without asserting a consumer exists for it.
dedupNotes: FOLDED two raw candidates sharing the SYA-not-repointed root cause: deploy F3 (migrate:ys-swap-deploy/idx2, root cause, Medium) and cleanup idx2 (the missing-VERIFICATION angle, Low). Auditors offered the choice to fold; folded here to avoid telling the reader the same gap twice while PRESERVING the cleanup-verification recommendation (the 'last gate should have caught it' angle is now the second half of the recommendation). Severity stays Medium (driven by the deploy-entry economic loss); the cleanup angle does not add severity, it adds a fix location.

title: gather-migration-inputs.js off-by-one: half-open getStakersRange treated as inclusive drops the last staker of every pool, making the leg1 (and leg2) count preflight permanently unsatisfiable (suite DoS) with misleading 're-run gather' guidance
location: scripts/gather-migration-inputs.js:271-284 (end = Math.min(start+PAGE_SIZE, countNum) - 1 passed as exclusive end); contract semantics lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:662-678 (getStakersRange half-open [start,end))
description: StableStaker.getStakersRange(token, start, end) returns the half-open slice [start, end) — its NatSpec says so. The gather script computes end = min(start+200, count) - 1 and passes it as if inclusive, so every page silently loses its final element; with counts <= 200 this is exactly the last staker of each pool. Empirically on a quiescent fork: DOLA fetched 2 of stakerCount 3 (dropped 0x25AdA296…), USDC fetched 5 of 6 (dropped 0x0f254C40…). The script then (a) prints a WARNING attributing the mismatch to 'stakers joined between reads' and advising a re-run — which can never converge because the bug is deterministic — and (b) writes count = fetched length into leg1-stakers.json. SkimAndLeg1Migration's preflight requires that count to equal live stakerCount exactly, so leg1 (preview AND broadcast) reverts 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count … re-run gather' forever. The SAME pager is used for --leg 2, so the gather for Leg2Migration against the temp staker inherits the identical block (count=2 DOLA / count=5 USDC), halting leg2 fail-loud at its own count-equality preflight.
impact: Hard, deterministic denial of the entire story-060 migration runbook at step 2 (and again at step 4) until the JS is fixed or the input file is hand-built. Fail-safe today only by accident of double-bookkeeping: had the script written the on-chain count instead of the fetched length, the preflight would pass and the dropped staker would be silently stranded in a terminally-migrating pool (recoverable only via permissionless userMigrate or a manual migrator batch). Operator time is also burned by the actively wrong 're-run' guidance.
evidence: side-effects.json inputGathering (gathered 2/3 and 5/6 on a quiescent fork; dropped addresses identified) and executed[0] (exact leg1 preflight revert). Input fixup #1 (hand-rebuilt JSON from getStakers()) immediately unblocks the preflight. leg2 recurrence: leg2-entry side-effects.json gatherResult + unmodifiedPreview revert 'Preflight: stale DOLA staker count in leg2-stakers.json - re-run gather', 2 != 3; leg2-stakers.BUGGY-LEG1-02.json captured.
recommendation: Use the half-open convention: const end = Math.min(start + PAGE_SIZE, countNum); pass end directly and advance start = end. Make the fetched-vs-count mismatch FATAL (process.exit(2)) rather than a non-fatal warning so the gatherer cannot emit an under-count file, and cross-check the final list against getStakers() when count <= a sanity bound. Applies identically to leg 1 and leg 2.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED leg1 idx1 (LEG1-02, canonical root cause, Medium) and leg2 idx1 (same code path against the temp staker, raw severity Low, self-labeled 'duplicate root cause of LEG1-02, do not double-count'). One root cause OffByOnePagination; leg2 recurrence folded as impact-scope evidence. Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Severity stays Medium (driven by the leg1 hard-DoS). The leg2 instance's fail-loud halt is the same defect reaching a second gate, not a new finding.

title: Leg2 re-deposit silently haircuts each user's principal by ~0.026% (DOLA) / ~0.016% (USDC); intent doc states principal is preserved 1:1
description: migrator2.migrate -> depositFor -> _routeDeposit deposits each migrating user's snapshot credit into the FIXED V2 ERC4626YieldStrategy, which (per story-060's own fix) credits convertToAssets(sharesReceived) rather than the nominal amount. The integer-rounding shortfall (received - credited) stays protocol-owned in the strategy, so each user's withdrawable principal on the original staker is strictly less than what they held on the temp staker. Measured on-fork: every DOLA position lost ~0.0260-0.0262% and every USDC position lost ~0.0157-0.0158%. The story-060 intent doc (User Impact) discloses the OLD-strategy (R,P) haircut but NOT this fresh re-deposit haircut introduced by the leg2 deposit into the new strategy.
impact: Real, permanent per-user principal reduction (small, uniform, proportional). Not a 1:1 round-trip as documented. Because tempStaker holds principal idle (no strategy), leg1's deposit was lossless, so this is a SINGLE fresh ERC4626 haircut, not compounded — but it is undisclosed value leakage from the user's perspective and accrues to the protocol/strategy buffer. NOTE: depends on YS-01 being fixed first (deposits revert until then); the haircut is the post-fix steady-state behavior.
evidence: side-effects.json perUserValuePreservation: DOLA total before 1033.6189 -> after 1033.3501 (loss 0.2688 DOLA, 0.0260%); USDC total before 1954.5707 -> after 1954.2630 (loss 0.3077 USDC, 0.0157%). yieldStrategy(DOLA)==yieldStrategy(USDC)==address(0) on temp confirms leg1 was lossless.
recommendation: Update the story-060 intent doc User Impact section to disclose that the leg2 re-deposit into the new ERC4626 strategy applies a small (~0.02-0.03%) conservative convertToAssets haircut to each position, distinct from the old-strategy (R,P) socialization. No code change required — the haircut is the correct conservative accounting; only the 1:1-preservation claim is inaccurate.
dedupNotes: Sole source: leg2 idx0. Distinct root cause (UndisclosedReDepositHaircut), no merge. Kept as standalone Low (doc-faithfulness).

title: Leg1/Leg2 staleness guard is count-equality only: equal-count membership drift between gather and broadcast slips the guard, strands the unlisted staker in a terminally-migrating pool, and the script is not re-runnable (initiateMigration is one-shot)
location: SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:146-157 (count-only check), :269-278 (post-assert); lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:425 (initiateMigration one-way). Leg2 instance: Leg2Migration.s.sol:126-136 (count-only require).
description: The preflight compares only .count against live stakerCount. If one staker exits and another enters between the gather snapshot and the broadcast (counts equal, membership different), preflight passes; the batch then processes the stale list — the departed address yields amount 0 (skipped) and the new staker is never migrated. The post-assert stakerCount==0 catches it, but in broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) it fires only AFTER all on-chain txs have landed: the pool is then in terminal Migrating state with one stranded staker, and re-running reverts at initiateMigration. Recovery is possible but undocumented (permissionless userMigrate, or manual migrator.migrate(token,[missed])). The same count-only weakness exists on the leg2 entry against the temp staker; the leg2 exposure is narrower because temp is a short-lived transit contract most users never touch directly, and the post-assert there also fails loud.
impact: Operational footgun: a benign user action in the gather->broadcast window can leave the migration half-finished on mainnet with no scripted recovery path. No funds lost (userMigrate exists); availability/runbook risk only. Probability low at the current 3/6-staker population.
evidence: Code reading of preflight + StableStaker terminal-migration semantics; story-055 ResumeStableStakerMigration as prior drift evidence (closure manifest cluster note). Not fork-demonstrated (would require staged user txs); analysis-supported. Leg2 instance: Leg2Migration.s.sol:126-136; stake/withdraw permitted while Active.
recommendation: Strengthen the guard: have gather store keccak256 of the sorted staker list and have preflight recompute it from getStakers() on-chain; or migrate from a fresh on-chain getStakers() read inside the script instead of a JSON snapshot (counts are tiny). For leg2, optionally freeze the transit temp staker before gather. Document the gather->broadcast no-new-stakes window and the userMigrate/manual-batch recovery in the runbook.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED leg1 idx3 (canonical, WeakDriftGuard) and leg2 idx3 (CountOnlyStalenessGuard, same root cause against the transit temp staker). One root-cause family (count-only staleness guard / snapshot-vs-broadcast drift). Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Both Low; the leg2 instance is narrower and folded as a cross-entry-point instance rather than a separate finding.

title: Skim proceeds diverge from the migration doc: sent to the original staker instead of the treasury, leaving ~13.5 USDe orphaned as idle staker balance and ~$3 of USDC+USDe parked on the phUSD minter via the old strategies' per-client buffer routing
location: SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-201 vs docs/stable-staker-migrations/yield-strategy-swap-June-12-2026.md:133-135, 224-234; buffer routing in deployed pre-story-025 bytecode at the 3 strategies
description: The intent doc's step 1a skims all three strategies to 'treasuryAddress'; its Post-Migration Options section reasons about surplus 'sitting at the treasury address as raw tokens'. The script instead skims to ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER, relying (per its post-assert comment) on ResetAndRewire's setYieldStrategy sweep to fold the idle balance into the V2 strategies as a principal buffer. That plan only covers DOLA and USDC: the USDe pool is never re-wired, so the USDe proceeds (~12.31 recipient share + ~1.19 staker buffer share = ~13.49 USDe) sit as unreserved idle balance on the staker indefinitely — reachable only via a manual StableStaker.rescueERC20 (StableStaker.sol:808) that no suite step performs. Additionally the DEPLOYED old-strategy bytecode routes each client's 25% set-aside buffer to the client contract itself (observed: 0.152660 USDC and 2.916739 USDe to the phUSD minter 0x435B0A18…), differing from the pinned ad12cb1 source and mentioned nowhere in story-060.
impact: Protocol-owned value scattered across unintended resting places: ~13.5 USDe orphaned on the staker (manual rescue required, undocumented), ~$3 on the phUSD minter. Doc-driven follow-ups ('option 2: re-inject from treasury') would target an address holding nothing. Non-obvious operator surprise (Law-3 footgun, low value at current scale); no user funds at risk.
evidence: side-effects.json stateWrites (USDe/USDC balance deltas incl. minter receipts), unintendedEffects, on-fork probe: setAsideBufferRecipient() selector reverts on deployed strategies while setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25.
recommendation: Update the migration doc to match the implemented destination and sweep plan; add an explicit step (cleanup is the natural place) that rescueERC20s the idle USDe to the intended treasury; document the minter-side buffer receipts or zero the buffers before skimming.
dedupNotes: Sole source: leg1 idx2. Distinct root cause (IntentDocDivergence). Standalone Low. Touches the same buffer-recipient and minter surfaces as YS-12 and YS-08 but the root cause (skim destination doc drift) is its own; cross-link only.

title: Set-aside buffer downgraded 25% -> 10% on replacement strategies: deploy script pins the intent doc's stale figure, contradicting the user-specified 25% set by replace-sya on the live strategies two days earlier
description: The intent doc (2026-06-12) claims 'the live original staker has a 10% set-aside buffer configured' and the script hardcodes SETASIDE_BUFFER=10 with a require pinning it. But ReplaceSYAMainnet (broadcast 2026-06-10) set STAKER_BUFFER_PERCENT=25 on all three live strategies, annotated 'USER-SPECIFIED 2026-06-10: 25%' — i.e. 10% was the pre-replace-sya value and 25% is the current deliberate choice. Verified on fork: old DOLA and USDC strategies both return setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25. The replacement strategies silently revert the staker's below-par insulation to 10% with no recorded rationale. Non-obvious owner footgun: the operator believes they are preserving existing protection while actually reducing it by 60%.
impact: Stakers' set-aside reserve against below-par dips is 10% of skimmed surplus instead of the currently-chosen 25%. Moot until YS-03 is fixed (no skims reach the new strategies at all), which compounds the configuration debt.
evidence: Fork reads: setAsideBufferSize(staker)==25 on 0x90ce…7F9 and 0x90af…470; ==10 on ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 after this script. ReplaceSYAMainnet.s.sol:132-136 comments. Intent doc 'Set-Aside Buffer' section. side-effects.json clusterChecks[2].
recommendation: Confirm the intended buffer with the owner; if 25% stands, change SETASIDE_BUFFER to 25 and source the value from the replace-sya decision in a comment. Update the stale figure in the intent doc.
dedupNotes: Sole source: deploy F4 (idx3). Distinct root cause (StaleConfigValue). Standalone Low.

title: ResetAndRewire broadcasts with --skip-simulation and a non-idempotent step sequence: the YS-01 deposit revert lands mid-suite on mainnet, leaving pools Active/strategyless/unpaused with no re-run path through the entry point
description: The broadcast entry uses --skip-simulation --slow, so forge sends txs one-by-one without a pre-broadcast bundle simulation. With the strategies as actually deployed (YS-01: previewRedeem reverts under STATICCALL), the mainnet run executes tx1 finalizeAndReset(DOLA) and tx2 finalizeAndReset(USDC) successfully then halts at tx3 setYieldStrategy(DOLA, ysDolaV2) with an on-chain reverted tx. Halt state: both pools revived to Active with yieldStrategy == address(0), migrator still migrator1, idle 26.785 DOLA + 27.234 USDC unswept, and 9 users parked yield-less in the temp staker. The entry point is NOT re-runnable after fixing the strategies: finalizeAndReset requires PoolState.Migrating, so tx1 reverts on every retry — and with --skip-simulation each retry burns another reverted mainnet tx. Worse, the halt window is publicly exposed: neither staker is paused and stake() on an Active strategyless pool succeeds, so ANY deposit (innocent or a 1-wei grief, ledger ss10l1) sets totalStaked > 0 and re-locks setYieldStrategy behind the story-010 empty-pool gate, forcing a full second terminal-migration cycle. A default forge simulation (no --skip-simulation) would have simulated the 6-tx bundle, hit the tx3 revert, and refused to send anything.
impact: Protocol availability + operational hazard, no direct fund loss: migration suite halts half-configured on mainnet; user principal stranded (recoverable) in temp until manual out-of-runbook recovery; recovery itself griefable via the story-010 gate during the unpaused halt window.
evidence: side-effects.json unmodifiedPreview (revert at tx3 with tx1/tx2 succeeding); StableStaker.finalizeAndReset require(poolState==Migrating) (StableStaker.sol:594); paused()==false on both stakers at post-state; story-010 gate at StableStaker.setYieldStrategy:228.
recommendation: 1) Drop --skip-simulation from all ys-swap broadcast entries. 2) Make the script resumable: guard each step (skip finalizeAndReset when poolState already Active; skip setMigrator when already set). 3) Pause both stakers for the migration window to close the public-stake gate-relock during any halt. 4) Run the preview variant against live mainnet immediately before broadcast as a hard runbook gate.
dedupNotes: Sole source: reset idx0. SAME family as YS-01 (the brick) but a DISTINCT root cause (NonResumableBroadcastWithSkipSimulation) — this is the script-level amplification (skip-simulation + non-idempotent ordering + unpaused halt window), not the vault-call bug. Kept distinct per the auditor's explicit framing ('THIS finding is the script-level amplification; the brick root cause is F1, referenced not duplicated'). Cross-linked to the --skip-simulation/non-idempotent operational family (YS-13) but kept Medium and separate because its halt-state is the most severe (mid-suite, on-chain, after users parked, gate-relock griefable) — NOT merged down into the Low operational-robustness family.

title: PostMigrationCleanup verify-5b USDC skim band reverts on the very state the migration produces, bricking the finalizer (temp minter never revoked)
description: The cleanup gate's per-token 'buffer sanity band' requires buffer = principalOf(token,original) - poolInfo(token).totalStaked to lie in [<token>Skimmed/2, <token>Skimmed*2], on the premise (comment L169-180) that buffer ≈ <token>Skimmed. That premise is false. The buffer is dominated NOT by the leg-1 skim but by the leg-1 initiateMigration realize-over-credit surplus: initiateMigration realizes the whole old-strategy position R into idle balance, exceeding credited P by accrued yield; ResetAndRewire's setYieldStrategy idle-sweep folds that whole excess into V2 principal. On the real post-migration fork state the USDC buffer is 27,229,913 (~27.2 USDC) while recorded usdcSkimmed is only 532,748 (~0.53 USDC) — 51.1x over the band's upper bound. The UNMODIFIED script REVERTS at 'Verify 5b FAILED: USDC buffer not within sanity band of usdcSkimmed' BEFORE the sole mutation, so phUSD.setMinter(tempStaker,false) never runs and the migration can never be declared COMPLETE. The DOLA pool has the same shape (~26.78 DOLA buffer) and escapes only because dolaSkimmed==0 disables its band branch — confirming the band, not the state, is wrong.
impact: The story-060 final step is non-functional against its own correctly-migrated mainnet state. Operators hit an unexplained revert at the finalizer; the temp staker retains live phUSD minter authorization indefinitely (a standing mint-capable surface the cleanup exists to remove); 'migration COMPLETE' is never signalled. Funds are not at risk and underlying state is solvent (principalOf > totalStaked on both pools), so this is availability/operational-integrity of the finalizer, not loss — Medium.
evidence: side-effects.json unmodifiedPreview: reverted=true, revertReason 'Verify 5b FAILED…', revertedBeforeMutation=true. bandMath: usdcBufferActual 27229913 vs band [266374,1065496], ratio 51.1x. FX4 variant (band removed, hard solvency kept) passes all 12 and revokes the minter — proving the band is the sole blocker. DOLA band SKIPPED only because dolaSkimmed==0.
recommendation: Drop the [skim/2, skim*2] band entirely and keep only the hard solvency invariant (principalOf >= totalStaked, already asserted at 4b/5b) — the real safety property; the script's own comment admits the band is 'diagnostic-only … inexact'. If a surplus sanity bound is desired, base it on the realize-over-credit accounting (leg-1 realized R minus credited P), not the skim alone, and log the ≈skim comparison rather than asserting it.
dedupNotes: Sole source: cleanup idx0. Distinct root cause (WrongPostConditionInvariant). Standalone Medium — a second independent suite-blocker (the finalizer reverts even after YS-01 etc. are fixed, on correct state). Not a duplicate of YS-01/YS-09.

title: Story-060 leaves migrator2 set on the live original staker after declaring migration COMPLETE — a standing terminal-migration footgun on a now-active pool
description: No story-060 script ever calls original.setMigrator(address(0)) (or any reset) after leg 2. PostMigrationCleanup revokes the temp staker's phUSD minter but neither clears nor verifies the migrator. On the fork, after cleanup, original.migrator() and tempStaker.migrator() both still return migrator2 (0xd263…FFfC), an immutable StableStakerMigrator(old=temp,new=original). Because StableStaker.initiateMigration is onlyMigrator, migrator2 remains an authorized path to terminally migrate the LIVE, repopulated original pool: a single owner call to migrator2.initiateMigration(DOLA/USDC) would freeze emissions, realize+decouple the V2 strategy, and set the pool active=true — irreversible (no resume path; ledger ss9l1) and thereafter exposing a PERMISSIONLESS userMigrate. The intent doc's 'Post-Migration Options' frames revocation as the expected terminal action; leaving the migrator standing after a step whose summary prints 'migration COMPLETE' is an undocumented, non-obvious privileged surface (Law-3 footgun), not the documented option-2 state.
impact: A non-malicious owner, believing the migration COMPLETE, retains a one-call irreversible bricking surface on a live, user-funded pool with permissionless follow-through. No unprivileged-attacker path and no fund loss absent owner action, so Low/QA — operational hazard for safe-config (Law 3).
evidence: side-effects.json preStateSummary + post-broadcast checks: original.migrator()==0xd263…FFfC and tempStaker.migrator()==0xd263…FFfC after cleanup. StableStaker.sol L148-149 onlyMigrator, L425 initiateMigration onlyMigrator nonReentrant, L555 userMigrate permissionless. StableStakerMigrator immutables old=temp/new=original. Doc 'Post-Migration Options' L224-235.
recommendation: Either (a) add original.setMigrator(address(0)) (and on temp) as an explicit step-6 action after the verifies, or (b) if option-2 re-injection is genuinely intended, have cleanup VERIFY the migrator is the expected migrator2 and emit a loud operator instruction that revocation is still pending — and document the standing privilege in the runbook. At minimum, cleanup should assert the post-migration migrator state it leaves behind.
dedupNotes: Sole source: cleanup idx1. Distinct root cause (MissingPostStepConfiguration / standing privilege). Standalone Low.

title: Deploy and leg2 broadcast entries are non-idempotent with no resume path: a halted/partial broadcast leaves half-wired or terminally-Migrating mainnet state, and re-running the documented command does not recover it
location: DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol:195-239 (no post-conditions, no resume); Leg2Migration.s.sol:188-217 (always calls initiateMigration first, no Active/Migrating branch)
description: Two related non-idempotent halt-states in the suite's operational robustness, distinct from the mid-suite reset halt (YS-09). (A) DEPLOY: the script's only guards are pre-flight; after 5 deployments and 11 mutations it asserts nothing and prints 'BROADCAST complete'. Under --skip-simulation + Ledger, a mid-sequence failure leaves e.g. phUSD.setMinter(temp,true) applied but migrators unset, with no idempotent re-run (re-running redeploys all five contracts, orphaning the JSON consumers' addresses). (B) LEG2: the broadcast uses --skip-simulation; if it halts after Step 1 initiateMigration(DOLA/USDC) but before all migrate chunks land, the temp pools are left in PoolState.Migrating, and re-running the SAME documented command reverts at the first action ('StableStaker: pool not active'). The migrate loop itself IS idempotent (batchMigrate skips amount==0), so a resume branch is feasible — it just isn't implemented. The project's own story-055 ResumeStableStakerMigration exists precisely because this failure mode is real.
impact: Operational: partially-wired or terminally-Migrating mainnet state with a stale/absent deployments JSON; recovery requires out-of-band cast calls (migrator2.migrate(token, remaining) for leg2; manual re-wire for deploy) under incident pressure. Funds not lost (idle pile + snapshot credit intact; migrate replay-safe per user).
evidence: Deploy: source lines 195-239 (no requires after wiring); intent.md 'Declared post-conditions: None'; sibling ResumeStableStakerMigration.s.sol (story 055). Leg2: StableStaker.sol initiateMigration require(poolState==Active) verified; Leg2Migration.s.sol always calls initiateMigration before the migrate loops with no Active/Migrating branch; batchMigrate skips amount==0 positions.
recommendation: Deploy: append a _postVerify() (pattern exists in ReplaceSYAMainnet.s.sol) re-reading every mutated slot and the five deployments before writing the JSON; add an idempotent guard that skips deployment if a valid ys-swap-deployments.json already exists. Leg2: add a resume-aware branch in run() — before Step 1, read tempStaker.poolState(token); if already Migrating, skip initiateMigration and proceed directly to the replay-safe migrate loop; optionally persist a progress.<chainId>.json marker.
dedupNotes: MERGED two raw Low candidates of one operational-robustness family: deploy F6 (idx5, MissingPostConditions / no-resume) and leg2 idx2 (NonIdempotentBroadcastNoResume). Both are non-idempotent-broadcast / no-resume halt-states with the same fix shape (resume-aware guards + post-conditions) and the same story-055 precedent. Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-deploy with leg2 as a cross-entry-point instance. The reset-entry instance is DELIBERATELY NOT merged here — it is YS-09 (Medium) because its halt lands mid-suite on-chain after users are parked and is griefable via the story-010 gate, a materially more severe halt-state than these two.

title: Reset preflight wires JSON-sourced strategy addresses and grants them unlimited token approval without any on-chain identity verification (code presence, vault, underlying, client authorization)
description: _globalPreflight checks only that ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2 are non-zero in ys-swap-deployments.json. It never verifies on-chain that (a) the addresses have code, (b) strategy.vault() is the expected autoDOLA/autoUSDC, (c) strategy.underlyingToken() matches the pool token, or (d) strategy.authorizedClients(ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER) == true — the doc's own 'Wire' checklist item ('setClient … needed for leg 2 re-deposit') that, if missed in step 1, makes tx3 revert AccessDenied mid-suite with the half-configured halt shape of YS-09. setYieldStrategy also grants the address an UNLIMITED token approval before the first compatibility check executes. Address drift in this file is not hypothetical: the closure manifest documents a preview-derived address (0x190cBd59…) colliding with live foreign mainnet code, and the deployments JSON is a mutable build artifact rewritten by step 1.
impact: Law-3 non-obvious footgun / weak drift guard. A stale, preview-contaminated, or mis-wired deployments JSON passes preflight and either halts the suite mid-broadcast (revert in the sweep deposit) or, if the foreign address tolerates the calls, leaves a max-allowance to an unvetted contract wired as the pool's strategy. No direct loss demonstrated; all observed fork values were correct.
evidence: side-effects.json preconditionResults (only non-zero checks present); doc 'Wire' checklist; closure-manifest.json unresolved[1] (0x190cBd… collision); cast verification this audit did manually (vault()/underlyingToken()/authorizedClients all checked out on the fork).
recommendation: Add to _globalPreflight, per strategy: require(addr.code.length > 0); require(IYS(addr).vault() == EXPECTED_VAULT && IYS(addr).underlyingToken() == token); require(IYS(addr).authorizedClients(ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER), 'setClient missing - run step 1 wiring'). Expected vault constants already exist in the doc.
dedupNotes: Sole source: reset idx1. Distinct root cause (MissingStrategyIdentityPreflight). Standalone Low.

title: PREVIEW_MODE env leakage silently turns the broadcast entry into a no-op that still patches mainnet-addresses.ts (zero-tx 'broadcast' exits 0, so the && chain runs the patcher)
description: Mode selection is an environment variable, not a CLI fact: if PREVIEW_MODE=true is still exported in the operator's shell (plausible — the runbook has the operator run the *-preview entries, and an export PREVIEW_MODE=true while iterating leaks into the broadcast invocation), `npm run migrate:ys-swap-reset` runs forge with --broadcast but the script takes the vm.startPrank branch, records ZERO broadcastable transactions, and — empirically verified on the fork — forge prints only 'Warning: No transactions to broadcast' and EXITS 0. The && chain then runs patch-mainnet-addresses-ys-swap.js, which unconditionally rewrites YieldStrategyDola/YieldStrategyUSDC in server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts. Result: the address registry (consumed by the UI/API) claims the V2 strategies are live while on mainnet the pools are still Migrating with no strategies wired and migrator1 in place.
impact: Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun: off-chain deployment registry desyncs from mainnet with exit-code success, misleading the UI and the operator's runbook checkpointing. No funds at risk directly; the on-chain system is simply not migrated.
evidence: Empirical probe (script taking the prank branch under --broadcast): forge exit code 0 with 'Warning: No transactions to broadcast'; patch script has no on-chain verification (trusts ys-swap-deployments.json only); ResetAndRewire.s.sol:174 envOr default false.
recommendation: Pin the env in package.json: `PREVIEW_MODE=false forge script …` (one-word fix), and/or derive mode from forge context (vm.isContext(ForgeContext.ScriptBroadcast)) rather than an env var. Additionally, have the patcher verify on-chain (eth_call: original.yieldStrategy(DOLA) == ysDolaV2) before rewriting the registry.
dedupNotes: Sole source: reset idx2. Distinct root cause (EnvFlagModeConfusion). Standalone Low.

title: Intent-doc / NatSpec / code three-way disagreement on the expected post-wire principal (doc: ==0; script header: >0; code: two-sided bound) — doc lag from the skim-parking decision
location: doc 'Step 3' (Verify: principalOf == 0); ResetAndRewire.s.sol:23-27 (header: principalOf > 0); :231-239 (code: principalOf <= idleSwept && (idleSwept==0 || principalOf>0))
description: The intent doc instructs the operator to verify YieldStrategyDolaV2.principalOf(DOLA, original) == 0 ('pool was empty before wiring'), written before the decision (leg1, commit 71c545c lineage) to PARK the skim surplus as idle balance on the staker and let setYieldStrategy fold it into the V2 strategies as an unattributed principal buffer. The script's NatSpec header says the opposite (principalOf > 0), and the code implements a third, correct, two-sided variant. Empirically the code is right (principal 26.778 DOLA / 27.229 USDC <= swept 26.785 / 27.234, both > 0) — but an operator cross-checking against the doc's '== 0' during a live broadcast would conclude the migration mis-fired. Minor: the doc splits 'Step 3 reset' and 'Step 4 wire migrator2' while the script merges both into one broadcast.
impact: Law-2 faithfulness / QA: stale runbook verification values can cause a false alarm (or train the operator to ignore verification mismatches) during a live migration. No on-chain impact; the coded asserts supersede the doc and passed on the fork.
evidence: side-effects.json postconditionResults; doc lines under 'Step 3 — Reset original and wire new strategies'; script NatSpec lines 23-27 vs code lines 231-239.
recommendation: Update the doc's Step-3 verification to the swept-idle bound (principalOf <= idle swept, > 0 when idle was non-zero) and renumber the doc steps to match the merged script; align the script header comment with its own code.
dedupNotes: Sole source: reset idx3. Distinct root cause (DocLagPostConditionContradiction). Standalone Low.
